title: Name the mismatch or unintended effect
subtitle: Inferences · 13 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **13 of the official questions in Inferences are this one** — 1 Easy, 3 Medium, 9 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The passage sets two things against each other: something seems simple but is demanding, a policy has a goal but also a loophole, one kind of work is easy to reach and another isn't.
- The blank follows 'there is a disparity between', 'the unintended effect of', 'those who ... risk' or 'Consequently'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Put the two sides of the contrast into your own words.
- 2) Choose the option that names that exact pair, or that states what naturally follows from the gap.
- For an unintended effect, it's usually the opposite of the policy's goal.
- 3) Check that both halves of the option match the passage.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick a choice that pairs the wrong two things, or that states only one side of the contrast.
For unintended-effect questions, you pick something that harms the side the policy already favours, when the answer is the harm to the side it was meant to protect.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
